A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MS-EDEN and Quartet II research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–D are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original quantization experiments, C4 and Nanochat training results, downstream evaluations, and GPU benchmarks in Sections 6–7 and the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains original training and quantization results and reports revised benchmark outcomes, repeated-run measurements, and additional B200 performance experiments.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 changes the correction factor from one per 128-element rotation group to one per 16-element quantization group, while retaining 128-element rotations. This modifies MS-EDEN's procedure without replacing its quantization principle or the Quartet II computation graph.

E1.justification: Reported downstream coverage changes substantially: Table 5 adds PIQA and HellaSwag and removes GSM8K, HumanEval, and MMLU evaluation results. ARC remains. C4, FineWeb-Edu, and the described fine-tuning datasets remain unchanged; removing GSM8K evaluation does not establish removal of its training use.

E2.justification: Figure 6 adds measured pure-GEMM performance ceilings as comparison references. The named training comparators remain BF16, NVIDIA, FourOverSix, and the same simplified TetraJet-v2 implementation; timing comparisons retain MXFP8 and Quartet.

E3.justification: Table 5 replaces post-SFT evaluations with pre-training few-shot, normalized evaluations and CORE scores. Appendix D revises the RTX 5090 BF16 baseline from micro-batch size 1 to batch size 4 using BF16 master parameters, and Table 7 changes profiling from 4096 to 8192 tokens per pass. V2 also introduces B200/OLMo2 configurations and forward-only timing experiments.

E4.justification: V2 adds forward-only speed measurements in Figure 10 and isolates quantization overhead using measured GEMM ceilings in Figures 6 and 10. It also expands the runtime breakdown in Table 7. The main forward/backward quantization ablations and gradient-concentration analysis remain.

E5.justification: V1 reports test-size-based, two-standard-deviation intervals only for the smaller BF16 model. V2 reports Quartet II variability from three pre-training runs in Figure 5 and Table 5, plus timing means and two-standard-deviation intervals over ten runs in Figures 6 and 10. These are substantial changes in uncertainty reporting; the previous run counts were unspecified.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises MS-EDEN MSE from 9.8 to 9.4 × 10^-3. Table 5 changes 560M Quartet II BPB from 0.7787 to 0.7790 and TetraJet-v2 from 0.7813 to 0.7825, while retaining the 1.9B BPB values and replacing downstream score rows. Under revised settings, RTX 5090 BF16/NVFP4 throughput changes from 20.8/51 to 28/52 ktok/s. New B200 end-to-end speedups range from 1.48× to 1.68×.

T1.justification: Appendix A adds a mathematical argument for the revised correction granularity by treating the 128-element RHT as 16-element rotations followed by further mixing. The existing Corollary 3.1 and asymptotic qualification remain; no new full theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the same central claims: unbiased MS-EDEN estimation with more than twofold lower quantization error, the fully-NVFP4 Quartet II graph, validation up to 1.9B parameters and 38B tokens, and kernel speedups up to 4.2×. The central conclusion is retained.

C2.justification: The conclusion newly discusses the restriction to LLM pre-training, NVFP4, and one accelerator generation, and qualifies generalization as potentially requiring further tuning. Section 7 adds explanations involving hardware ceilings and quantization overhead, including the lack of B200 speedup at the smallest tested size.

D1.justification: V2 specifies the clipping factor s = (1/0.93) × 6 × (16/17), clarifies per-tensor/per-micro-batch rotation randomization, and discloses the externally supplied abs-max assumption for layer benchmarks. It changes the reported GEMM backend from QuTLASS to cuBLAS and documents additional B200 settings. The code link and core hyperparameter tables remain.

R1.justification: V2 adds references for PIQA, HellaSwag, OLMo2, and an NVIDIA throughput comparison, while removing the HumanEval, MMLU, and QuTLASS references. Section 2's substantive positioning against previous quantization methods remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most of the abstract, introduction, method exposition, and experimental narrative is retained. Changes are concentrated in the kernel discussion and appendices, the expanded Conclusion and Limitations section, and a new Impact Statement, funding acknowledgments, and publication header.

P2.justification: V2 substantially redesigns the empirical displays: Figure 5 is enlarged and gains uncertainty bands and corrected token units; Figure 6 gains separate GPU panels, error bars, and GEMM ceilings; Figure 10 is new. Table 5 becomes stacked model-specific panels with an interval column, and Table 7 adds absolute timings and revised categories. Several existing displays are relocated.

improvement.justification: Repeated-run uncertainty, B200 measurements, the revised BF16 timing baseline, and explicit implementation assumptions improve the evidence and reproducibility. The gains are qualified by lost post-SFT evidence and editorial inconsistencies: Section 6.2 still describes those removed results, and Section 7 overstates small-model RTX 5090 speedups relative to Figure 6. Overall, the added transparency supports a limited quality improvement.
